goalbuddy_receipt_v1.rationale: Focused tests and Codex verification pass, but the temporal graph is not ready. Remote projection acknowledgements may omit the expected hash yet still create a complete checkpoint, so KG-AC08 is proven only for the in-memory engine. More seriously, upsert persists claims and entities before validating all relation targets, allowing rejected or interrupted mutations to leave partial canonical truth that a rebuild can project. Relation IDs are not canonically workspace-bound, and malformed Graphiti query responses bypass direct fallback. These violate backend equivalence and canonical-authority guarantees despite otherwise sound encryption, temporal history, bounded queries, revalidation, and tombstone ordering.

worker_package.objective: Repair the T005 temporal graph as one atomic vertical slice: preflight every claim, entity, relation, closure, target, collision, temporal window, provenance/admission reference, and canonical workspace-scoped ID before mutation; make each upsert, contradiction, and supersession atomically visible through an immutable commit/batch mechanism so failed validation or crashes cannot expose partial canonical truth to canonicalState, query, projection, or rebuild; require every remote projection acknowledgement to contain the exact expected projection_hash before recording a complete checkpoint; prove remote rebuild equivalence after backend loss; and make invalid as well as thrown Graphiti project/query responses use the authenticated parameterized direct-Neo4j fallback followed by canonical revalidation. Preserve existing encryption, tombstone-first revocation, typed-AST bounds, deterministic behavior, and T005-only scope.
stop_if: The repair requires changing files outside allowed_files, adding dependencies, live credentials, deployment, router/MCP behavior, or T006 ontology/improvement behavior.
Atomic visibility cannot be achieved while preserving recoverable encrypted canonical records and compatibility with the existing vault without a separately approved migration.
A crash at any injected point can still make an uncommitted claim, entity, relation, closure, or replacement visible to query, projection, or rebuild.
A remote backend cannot return and verify the exact canonical projection hash under the documented graphd contract.
The same verification failure recurs twice without new evidence.

evidence: The focused graph and ontology suite passed 10/10; npm run verify:codex and git diff --check also passed on 2026-08-04.

scripts/lib/knowledge-graph-adapter.mjs accepts a remote project response when ok is true and projection_hash is absent, then records the checkpoint as complete; the direct-fallback test explicitly returns only {ok:true}.
KG-AC08 clears and rebuilds the deterministic in-memory engine, but no test proves Graphiti/direct-Neo4j loss recovery with a mandatory matching remote hash or rejection of missing/mismatched hashes.

upsertEpisodeGraph persists the claim and entities before validating all supersede/contradict targets and relation operations; no batch commit marker prevents those revisions from becoming canonical after a later failure or crash.
Relation validation accepts caller-supplied nonempty relation IDs without verifying the canonical workspace-scoped derivation.
Graphiti query fallback covers thrown primary errors, but response-shape validation occurs after the fallback try block, so malformed primary responses do not invoke direct fallback.

Exact-source review confirmed encrypted immutable revisions, admission/provenance revalidation, default-three/hard-five typed queries, temporal closing, deterministic IDs for entities/claims, authoritative tombstone-first removal, and canonical result filtering.

parallel_safety.rationale: The repair changes shared canonical mutation, projection, fallback, and test surfaces; splitting it would risk incompatible transaction and acknowledgement semantics.

missing_evidence: Atomic all-or-nothing visibility for failed validation and crash points throughout upsert, contradiction, and supersession.
Mandatory matching projection hashes from Graphiti and direct-Neo4j acknowledgements, including missing-hash and mismatch rejection.
Remote backend-loss rebuild equivalence rather than only in-memory-engine equivalence.
Canonical workspace binding and deterministic validation for caller-supplied relation IDs.
Direct fallback after malformed, not only thrown, Graphiti project and query responses.
required_board_updates: Record T016 as rejected with the focused verification pass and the listed canonical-atomicity/backend-equivalence defects.
Do not activate T006; insert the graph-repair Worker package before ontology automation and continuous improvement.
Require a new milestone audit of the repaired T005 slice before unblocking T006-T008.
